title: Forced Circulation Evaporator
model_title: Forced Circulation Evaporator (Heater + Flash Separator + Circulation Pump)

introduction.definition: A forced circulation evaporator pumps the liquid at high velocity through a heat exchanger and back to a separator. Because of the static head above the exchanger the liquid is only heated, not boiled, in the tubes; it flashes when it reaches the lower-pressure separator. This prevents scale and crystal deposits on the heating surface.
key_points: Large circulation pump (high flow, low head)

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Temperature rise per pass ~ 2–5 °C; circulation rate ≫ evaporation rate.

temperature.title: Hydrostatic head suppresses boiling in the tubes
temperature.description: The circulation pump drives liquid through the tubes at high velocity (typically ~ 1.5–3 m/s). The static head above the tubes keeps the liquid under enough pressure that it is only heated (a few °C) without boiling; it flashes when it reaches the separator. Suppressing boiling at the wall prevents scaling and crystal deposition — ideal for crystallising, scaling or viscous liquids.

foundation: Support vessels on structure/legs designed for operating and flooded weights; allow thermal growth of calandrias and vapour lines.
alignment: Vertical calandrias plumb (falling-film distribution depends on it); slope liquor lines for drainage.
piping: Vapour lines sized for low ΔP; condensate drained by traps or level control; vents for non-condensables on each steam chest.
Vacuum system (condenser + vacuum pump/ejector) for the last effect.
commissioning: Leak/vacuum test; water trials (wetting, levels); bring steam on slowly; set levels and densities; CIP routine.

causes: Low static head or high ΔT

safety: Hot, pressurised slurry; lock out pump before opening loop.

video_tutorials.title: Forced Circulation Evaporator — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Forced Circulation Evaporator.
A forced circulation evaporator pumps the liquid at high velocity through a heat exchanger and back to a separator.
Because of the static head above the exchanger the liquid is only heated, not boiled, in the tubes; it flashes when it reaches the lower-pressure separator.
This prevents scale and crystal deposits on the heating surface.
Typical applications include crystallisation (salts, sodium sulphate); scaling and viscous liquids; wastewater zero-liquid-discharge concentrators.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Heat Exchanger Shell (steam side), Inlet & Outlet Heads, Axial/Mixed-Flow Circulation Pump & Motor (high flow, low head), Pump Impeller.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Forced Circulation Evaporator — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Forced Circulation Evaporator.
Monitor pump amps, ΔT and slurry density.
Check tube velocity and scaling; flush.
Inspect pump impeller and tubes for erosion.
Watch for erosion by crystals: thinning tubes, impeller wear. Common cause: high velocity slurry.
Watch for boiling in tubes (scaling): rapid fouling. Common cause: low static head or high δt.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
